key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel, higher-velocity spray processes produced denser, harder coatings with much better wear and corrosion performance than atmospheric plasma spraying.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical surfaces, HVOF and HVAF are the strongest choices here, with HVAF giving the best overall corrosion resistance and top-tier wear resistance.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr cemented carbide coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure, hardness, tribological behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance were compared across the four spray routes.
Wear tracks and corrosion metrics were used to identify dominant degradation mechanisms and process-performance tradeoffs.
evidence_signal: Compared with 304 stainless steel, coating hardness increased to 771.4–1166.2 HV, wear rate dropped from 36.82×10^-5 to 1.10–7.93×10^-5 mm3/N·m, friction coefficient fell from 0.68 to 0.43–0.56, and HVAF showed the best corrosion results (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: Results are specific to this coating chemistry, substrate, and test conditions, so process selection should still account for part geometry, cost, residual stress, and service environment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
